result.rationale: parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts explicitly does `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"; }`. In office365calendar CalendarService, `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }` spreads the fabricated literal over stored credentials, then persists it via prisma.credential.update — destroying the real refresh_token so future refreshes fail. The mechanism is verifiable in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `parseRefreshTokenResponse` which, when the parsed token data lacks `refresh_token`, mutates the parsed result by setting `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-29). In Office365 refresh, the returned parsed data is merged over existing credentials: `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) };` (packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts). If credential sharing mode is enabled (minimum schema used, which does not require/expect `refresh_token`), this will inject the literal and then overwrite the real stored `refresh_token` during the prisma update, permanently corrupting the credential.
